2030 Goal: Reduce Scope 1 & 2 emissions by 65% vs. 2010 baseline
Perspective / Path Forward (summary): We continue to make strong progress, having already exceeded our original goal of 50% and are increasing it to 65%. We have significantly reduced our Scope 2 emissions via the purchase of renewable electricity and have a longstanding focus on increasing energy efficiency. This has driven both cost savings and reductions in Scope 1 and will continue to do so going forward. Finding cost-effective thermal energy solutions for Scope 1 emissions remains a challenge; P&G helped form the Renewable Thermal Collaborative with WWF to advance renewable thermal energy solutions across the industry.

P&G is on track to achieve >99% purchased renewable electricity and is focusing on opportunities that support bringing additional renewable capacity online, while exploring cost-effective solutions to address the remaining <1%.

2030 Goal: Reduce supply chain (Scope 3) emissions by 40% per unit of production vs. 2020 baseline
Perspective / Path Forward (summary): P&G continues to pursue material efficiency, increased use of recycled/renewable materials, low-carbon alternatives, and renewable energy/carbon capture in its supply chain, including investments with key suppliers projected to reduce several million metric tons of CO2 over the next decade (CCS/CCU, hydrogen utilization, bio-based solutions, renewable energy). Industry-wide challenges outside P&G's direct control (low-carbon solution viability, energy infrastructure, evolving carbon accounting guidelines) represent sources of uncertainty. P&G estimates about three-quarters of this goal may be feasible by 2030.

2030 Goal: Reduce upstream finished product freight emission intensity by 50% vs. 2020 baseline
Perspective / Path Forward (summary): P&G reversed a 4% increase (from the 2020 baseline) recorded in 2022 into a 4% decrease by 2024 — a gross reduction of 8% — driven by container fill rates, intermodal transport, and optimized distribution routes. Further reductions depend on alternative-fuel vehicle transportation infrastructure not yet available at scale, an industry-wide constraint tied to future policy developments.

2030 Goal: 100% of consumer packaging designed to be recyclable or reusable
Perspective / Path Forward (summary): Strong progress continues via packaging design work and scaling recycling infrastructure with value-chain partners. Remaining industry-wide challenges concern small-size packaging (under 2x2 inches) and flexible packaging, which require at-scale solutions not yet in place and that may not exist by 2030. P&G is part of a cross-sector coalition on small-size packaging and The Recycling Partnership's Flexibles and Films Coalition. P&G estimates the share of its packaging portfolio without feasible at-scale technical solutions by 2030 to be in the low single digits.

2030 Goal: Reduce virgin petroleum plastic in consumer packaging by 50% per unit of production vs. 2017 baseline
Perspective / Path Forward (summary): Progress driven by a multi-faceted strategy: lighter packaging, increased use of recycled materials, and increased use of plastic alternatives. P&G states it is currently on track to achieve this goal by 2030.

2030 Goal: Increase water efficiency at P&G facilities by 35% per unit of production vs. 2010 baseline
Perspective / Path Forward (summary): Facilities maintain a sustained focus on driving water efficiency, with strong progress to date; P&G states it is currently on track for the 2030 goal.

2030 Goal: Recycle and reuse 5 billion liters of water in P&G facilities annually
Perspective / Path Forward (summary): P&G has identified innovative site-level solutions to continue significant progress and states it is currently on track for the 2030 goal.

2030 Goal: Restore more water than consumed at manufacturing sites in 18 water-stressed areas (+ Mexico City & LA product-use water)
Perspective / Path Forward (summary): P&G is working with a network of on-the-ground partners on long-term projects that improve, manage, or protect freshwater sources. Currently identified projects are expected to deliver 22% of the goal; the remaining 78% will come from projects not yet identified. P&G states it is on track, but notes natural disturbances (extreme weather, fire, etc.) could affect individual projects and results.

2030 Goal: Provide 25 billion liters of clean drinking water via Children's Safe Drinking Water program (target: 2025)
Perspective / Path Forward (summary): P&G has provided 23 billion liters of clean water through the Children's Safe Drinking Water program to date and states it is on track to achieve the 25-billion-liter goal.

2030 Goal: 100% of palm oils used in P&G brands RSPO certified
Perspective / Path Forward (summary): P&G continues to maintain 100% RSPO certification covering palm oils used in its brands. Supply constraints persist for RSPO-certified palm kernel oil specifically, though the maintenance goal continues to be met overall.

2030 Goal: 100% of sourced wood pulp certified by a globally recognized system
Perspective / Path Forward (summary): P&G continues to maintain 100% of sourced wood pulp certified by a globally recognized third-party certification system.

2030 Goal: 100% of paper packaging recycled or third-party certified virgin content
Perspective / Path Forward (summary): P&G continues to make progress toward this goal and anticipates maintaining these results going forward. Figure is based on supplier self-reported data; responses received by report publication represented 95% of total supply volume, and P&G does not expect the remaining share to materially affect reported results.

2030 Goal: 50% of virgin paper packaging FSC certified (original target year: 2025)
Perspective / Path Forward (summary): P&G states it has exceeded this original goal (which had a 2025 target year) and will maintain its preference for FSC certification going forward.

2030 Goal: Protect, restore or improve more than 1.5 million acres of land
Perspective / Path Forward (summary): P&G has completed development of its land-protection project portfolio in partnership with conservation organizations; projects currently in the portfolio are expected to deliver the full 1.5-million-acre goal once fully implemented. P&G notes natural disturbances (extreme weather, fire, etc.) could affect individual projects and results.

2030 Goal: Advance Natural Climate Solutions to balance manufacturing emissions not eliminated this decade
Perspective / Path Forward (summary): P&G has worked with a network of NGO partners to develop a project portfolio expected to deliver 86% of this goal once fully implemented, focused on projects delivering carbon benefits alongside positive impacts on people and nature. P&G states it is currently on track, noting natural disturbances or changes to carbon accounting could affect individual projects and results.
